comment: REVIEWED RETRY-SHAPE SITES — the ONLY suppression mechanism for arm (iii) of
checks/check_order_path_bans.py. Read that gate's docstring before adding a row.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Arm (iii) detects hand-rolled retry SHAPES structurally, and it is
deliberately biased toward flagging: a flagged legitimate loop is recoverable, a missed retry
sends two orders at the venue with real money (risk spec v1.3 §2A:71, §4:241, §12A:830 — the
system NEVER auto-resends). Bias toward flagging means false positives, and a false positive
with no way to record a review turns into pressure to widen the detector until it is quiet.
That widening is the failure this file exists to prevent.
WHAT A SUPPRESSION IS. One reviewed SITE. The key is (file, qualname, shape, verb) — all four
must match or the suppression does not apply.
WHAT A SUPPRESSION IS NOT, and these are structural, not conventions:
* NOT file-level. There is no `file`-only form; `qualname`, `shape` and `verb` are required
keys and an entry missing any of them is REJECTED and reported as a violation.
* NOT directory-level. No path prefix or glob is honoured anywhere in the gate.
* NOT a blanket. `shape` must be one of the gate's named retry shapes; a suppression cannot
silence the retry-LIBRARY or loop-BLOCKING-call arms at all.
* NOT line-keyed. `debug.md` §8 failure mode #4 is the stale literal anchor and a line number
is one. Reformat the file and the suppression still holds; move the code to another
function and it stops holding, which is the correct behaviour.
SELF-EXPIRING. An entry matching NO site in the current tree is a VIOLATION, not a no-op. A
review applies to code that exists; when the code moves, the review is owed again. An entry
with an empty `justification` or `reviewed_in` is also a VIOLATION — an unsigned suppression
is not a review.
VISIBLE ON EVERY RUN. Every applied suppression is printed in the gate's `evidence` as
`ADVISORY ... (REVIEWED SUPPRESSION — <justification>)`. A suppression can go stale but it
cannot go invisible.
MEASURED FALSE-POSITIVE RATE — a DATED measurement, ARC 018, against the tree at b8ba7ff.
Arm (iii) produced 1 hit across 4 in-scope files holding 9 loop constructs. 1 hit, 1 false
positive, 1 row below; the other 8 loops cleared with no row and no suppression. Rate = one
review owed per 4 order-path files. The gate is usable at that rate. Re-derive rather than
trusting this line — it is history, and history is append-only:
.venv/bin/python checks/check_order_path_bans.py    (every hit and every applied
suppression is printed in `evidence` on every run). If a future arc finds the rate
climbing, the correct response is to SAY SO, not to add rows until the gate is quiet.
NEGATIVE TEST CASE. ARC 018 sub-agent B's `ib_reject_category()` — a classification loop over
an IB_REJECT_RULES table, the first new loop in scripts/broker/ since the detector was
designed — was planted verbatim and cleared BY CONSTRUCTION (no send verb in the body), with
the walker confirmed to have seen the loop. No row was added for it, and none is owed.

reviewed.justification: FAN-OUT, NOT RETRY. `flatten(all)` iterates the position mirror and issues ONE market close per SYMBOL; the client_order_id is `flat-{sym}-{seq}` so every iteration is a distinct order for a distinct instrument. The loop's cardinality is the number of open positions, not a retry budget, and no symbol is sent twice. RE-REVIEWED ARC 020, AND THE RE-REVIEW WAS OWED RATHER THAN OPTIONAL: the ARC 018 row keyed this site to verb `place_order`, and ARC 020's D1.27(a)/D1.28 work extracted the send into `_emit_flatten_leg()`, so the old row went stale and the gate reported it as a VIOLATION. That is this file's self-expiring rule working exactly as written — the code moved, so the review was owed again — and the row is re-signed rather than re-pointed. WHAT WAS RE-VERIFIED, not carried over: (1) `_emit_flatten_leg` contains NO loop; it sends exactly once per call, so the retry shape lives only in the caller's per-symbol fan-out. (2) The `except Exception` handler inside `_emit_flatten_leg` RETURNS a `(symbol, reason)` failure tuple and never re-invokes `place_order`; the caller collects failures and continues, then raises once with the full picture (the ARC 015 protective-path defect fix). The `re_review_if` trigger below is therefore explicitly NOT met. (3) The loop bound is still the position mirror. ARC 020 added two `continue` arms ahead of the send — the idempotency-window suppression and the unheld-symbol no-op — and both can only REDUCE the number of sends per pass, never increase it, so the fan-out's upper bound is unchanged at one order per open position. Re-verified against risk spec §2A `flatten(symbol | all)`: fanning out over `all` is the specified behaviour of the verb.
reviewed.reviewed_in: ARC 018 sub-agent C (D2.14); re-reviewed and re-signed ARC 020 Phase 4 after the send moved behind _emit_flatten_leg
reviewed.re_review_if: the handler ever calls place_order or _emit_flatten_leg (that is shape except_reinvokes_send and this suppression does not cover it), or the loop bound stops being the position mirror, or _emit_flatten_leg acquires a loop of its own
